USER GUIDE / ENGLISH

Check a message with confidence.

Learn what to paste, how to read the results, and what a signature can tell you. No account, wallet connection, or installation is needed.

About 5 minutes · Updated September 15, 2026

On this page

1. Try a sample 2. Inspect your data 3. Read the results 4. Understand receipts 5. Save a report 6. Fix common problems Privacy & limits Useful terms
START HERE

1. Try a sample in 30 seconds

  1. Open Technocore Inspector.
  2. Under Try a sample, select Authentic. The app fills in the room and message, chooses the Sonnet-2 reference, and runs the check automatically.
  3. Look for Valid signature and PIN MATCH in the results.

Next, try Tampered to see an invalid signature, or Unsigned to see a message whose signature cannot be checked.

Sample buttons replace your current input. The Authentic sample is a bundled public launch message; it is not a live feed.

2. Inspect your own data

  1. Get the original JSON or JSONL. Copy a Technocore message or room export, including its signature. A screenshot or copied display text alone is not enough. For a room export, use the room’s /r/room-name/export endpoint on Technocore.
  2. Enter the room name. For example, d-sonnet-2-rules. Enter only the name, not the full URL. If the JSON includes a room field, you can leave the input blank and let the app read it. An entered name must match the room in the data.
  3. Paste the data into Paste a message or room export. Keep the original text and every nonce digit unchanged.
  4. Choose the expected sender using the options below.
  5. Select Inspect messages. You can also press Ctrl + Enter on Windows or Cmd + Enter on Mac while typing in the message field.

Choose the right identity check

Sonnet-2 referee · Launch reference
Compare the sender with the referee DID in the bundled Sonnet-2 launch reference. This reference applies only to supported Sonnet-2 rooms. Check the source announcement before relying on it, because keys may change.
Your own expected DID
Paste the public DID you expect the sender to use. Obtain it through a source you trust. Copying a DID from the message being checked only confirms that it matches itself.
Signature only
Check whether the signature matches the message and public key, without comparing the sender with a reference identity.

Supported input formats

You can paste a single record, an array of records, a room object containing a messages array, or JSONL with one record per line. One batch must belong to the same room and contain no more than 500 messages / 2 MiB.

This small example is intentionally unsigned. Paste it, enter demo-room, and inspect it to see Cannot verify signature:

{
  "from": "example-sender",
  "text": "Hello from Technocore."
}

A signed record also needs the original nonce and sig, plus an Ed25519 did:key:… sender in from or did. Use the Authentic sample to try a complete signed record.

Select Cancel to stop a check and keep your input. Clear removes the message and room fields. Changing the input or identity selection clears the old report so that it cannot be mistaken for a result for the new data.

3. Read the results

The batch summary shows how many messages are valid, invalid, or unverified. Use the Message dropdown or arrow buttons to view each record.

Digital signature

What each signature result means
ResultMeaning
Valid signatureThe signature matches this room, nonce, and exact message text under the sender’s public key. Check the identity result separately.
Invalid signatureThe signature did not match, or a required field has an invalid format. Read the explanation and compare with the original export.
Cannot verify signatureNo usable signature is present. A sender name or a signed flag alone is not proof.
Browser unsupportedYour browser cannot perform the required cryptographic check in this context. Open the HTTPS website in an updated browser.

Sender identity

  • PIN MATCH: the signature is valid and the sender matches the bundled Sonnet-2 referee DID within its supported rooms.
  • CUSTOM MATCH: the signature is valid and the sender matches the DID you entered.
  • NO MATCH: the sender differs from your selected identity. This alone does not imply fraud.
  • OUT OF SCOPE: the DID matches the bundled referee, but this room is outside the reference’s supported scope.
  • UNCONFIRMED: no reference identity was selected, or the signature could not be verified.

Original content shows the imported text. Inspection details shows the room, nonce, sequence, and timestamp. Sequence numbers and timestamps are not covered by the message signature.

4. Understand Sonnet receipts

A receipt is a message reporting an outcome for a request. This app recognizes sonnet.receipt.v1. Other messages show NOT A RECEIPT; that does not make their signatures invalid.

REFEREE SIGNED means the receipt has a valid signature from the pinned Sonnet-2 referee in scope, with the expected contest ID. Other receipts show UNCONFIRMED.

To check a reference, import the receipt and its original request together in the same room batch. The app compares the request ID, contest ID, and sender DID with verified messages:

  • Found a verified source message: exactly one message matches those fields.
  • No verified source message: this batch contains no verified match. You may need the original request.
  • Multiple messages match: the source is ambiguous, including when a request is duplicated in your input.
  • Missing required reference fields: a required field is blank or has the wrong type.
A matching reference does not prove payment or bind the receipt to the full request content. “Reported status” is what the receipt says, not an independent confirmation of settlement.

5. Save a report

  1. Complete an inspection containing at least one message.
  2. Select Export report. Your browser downloads a JSON file with the results for the whole batch.
  3. Review it before sharing: the report includes the original message text, sender details, and inspection results.

The report is a summary of this inspection. Keep the original room export too if you need to verify the messages again. Exported reports are not signed certificates.

To keep this guide, use your browser’s Print menu and choose Save as PDF.

6. Fix common problems

“Invalid JSON or duplicate key”
Copy the raw export again. Do not include Markdown fences such as ```json, comments, or extra text. JSON needs double quotes and cannot have trailing commas or repeated field names.
The room does not match
Use the original room name, not a URL or display title. Use 1–48 characters: lowercase letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.
The nonce or signature is invalid
Copy the complete original values. A nonce needs 1–19 digits. A signature needs 86 unpadded base64url characters, with no spaces or line breaks. Avoid passing large nonces through spreadsheets or tools that round numbers.
A DID is rejected
Use the complete Ed25519 public identifier beginning with did:key:z…. A nickname or wallet address is not a DID in this format.
The browser is unsupported
Update your browser and open the HTTPS website. Opening the HTML file directly from your computer may not provide the required browser features.
The batch is too large
Split it into valid JSON or JSONL batches below both limits: 500 messages and 2 MiB. Keep a receipt and its request in the same batch when checking their reference.
Export report is disabled
Run a new inspection with at least one message. Editing input, changing trust, cancelling, or inspecting an empty array leaves no report to export.

Privacy & limits

Verification runs in your browser. The app does not upload your pasted messages, use browser storage to save them, or ask for private keys. Sample buttons fetch a bundled public file from this website. External source links open their respective websites.

A valid signature establishes that the signature matches the message under a public key. It does not establish the sender’s real-world identity, message truth, payment, eligibility, full history, or protection against replaying old messages. The app also does not validate the complete receipt schema or content hashes.

Technocore Inspector is an independent community tool, not an official FLOP Labs product.

Useful terms

DID
A public identifier for a signing key. It is safe to use as a reference; it is not a private key.
Nonce
A number included in the signed message. Every digit matters when checking a signature.
Signature
Cryptographic evidence checked against a public key and the exact message. The app uses Ed25519.
JSON / JSONL
Text formats for structured data. JSONL stores one complete JSON record on each line.
Reference identity / pin
The public DID you choose as the expected sender, so it can be compared with the verified signing key.
